explanation: The M230L substitution reduces efavirenz binding through a subtle loss of van der Waals contact complementarity at the NNRTI pocket rim. Methionine's longer, flexible sulfur-containing side chain makes optimized hydrophobic contacts with efavirenz at the 2.7 Å interface, whereas leucine's shorter branched aliphatic side chain cannot maintain the same contact surface despite minimal volume loss, creating a local binding pocket deficit. This conformational mismatch propagates from the pocket rim inward, destabilizing the inhibitor's binding pose without requiring steric clash or electrostatic perturbation.
